title: Bloody Usaunny
text: Balloons were decently mid-tier fodder, but they were never treated as mascots, I say. Filolial-sama did exist even under a different name, but was strictly treated as a mount or an ordinary monster. Hii… memories of my game-era self going hunting with the swine, calling it “duck hunting,” came flooding back. Ah, b-but that was the game. Yes, that was the game, not the actual Filolial-sama, I say.
“Come to think of it, there’s a Usapiru boss, isn’t there? If we keep going, are we gonna fight that boss from the game?”
“The Usapiru boss? What’s it like? Something like… King Usapiru?”
“Nope, it was named Ro-Spiru. Not that strong a boss, though.”
“Heh.”
“Looks-wise it’s a big Usapiru, but it brings along a retinue of Usapiru. It dropped enhancement materials, so it was definitely a worthwhile monster to fight.”
“The drop item was a tool called a Magic Clover, indeed.”

Talking about game knowledge brought back fond memories, I say. Ah, back in that first world—looking back now, I wish I’d told Father so much more about all this. Just a little anecdote that comes to mind.
“Usapiru, huh. Speaking of which, Balloons too—you can raise monsters using monster crests, you know. If you raised something like a Usapiru, would it grow up weird like the Filolials do?”
“What kind of growth would that be, I wonder. A rabbit monster…”
“The classic powerful rabbit monster people think of, in games, is that one, right? The one that fires instant-death attacks.”
“I’ve heard of that one. Gets used a lot.”
“Apparently that originally came from some comedy movie, but it exists in Ren’s and Itsuki’s worlds too, huh. If anything, there might be some connection to Ren, the Sword Hero?”
“Why’s that?”
“Well, it’s a comedy movie premised on the protagonist being the guy who pulled out a famous holy sword. If anything, that sword is the famous one. Excalibur—does that ring a bell?”
“The ‘comedy’ part is what worries me here.”

“Well… after that, it got incorporated into a lot of games as a vicious rabbit trope. By the way, the Vorpal thing is actually unrelated to rabbits in Through the Looking-Glass. Well, rabbits do show up in that work, but it’s a coined term.”
And so Father explained all sorts of little details to us, I say.
“If we raised a Usapiru, would it grow into a monster like that?”
“There’s a rabbit right here that deals fatal blows,” Itsuki said, looking at me, I say.
“HAHAHA! For this Motoyasu, dealing fatal blows to whatever enemy appears is child’s play, I say.”
“Well… yeah. Motoyasu-kun does seem like he’d casually deal fatal blows to just about anyone.”
“Bloody Usaunny, huh. Can’t deny that red suits you.”

Ren’s mysterious push for red, I say. Admittedly, I too am fond of red attire. Though I’m also partial to green, incidentally. I made good use of it during the first wave, mindful of efficiency. Naturally, one changes outfits depending on the situation. Come to think of it… there was a time when Father kept a rabbit demi-human. That’s a memory from a loop where I failed to save her and let Itsuki take the blame for a false accusation, I say. Judging by the weapon she carried, her attack style seemed to be that of a slave built for delivering fatal blows, if I recall.
“Back to the Usapiru topic—the Balloons and Usapiru that Father took care of in the first world were… modified by Father into Raph-species.”
At my words, Ren and Itsuki swiftly put some distance between themselves and Father, I say.
“Hold on, Motoyasu-kun!”
“Raph-species… you mean like Raph-chan, modeled after Big Sister? They got remade into monsters like that?”
“That’s a horrifying story.”
“No, the monsters being kept volunteered to change their forms, so they seemed fairly happy about it, I say.”
“Is that supposed to make it better…?”
Ah, well, that lively version of Father back then was also a possibility of who Father could be, I say.
“I wonder if simply raising them just naturally led to the monster Itsuki mentioned?”
“From what I recall, it did end up looking close enough to the monster Itsuki described, I say.”
“Guess hero correction really does make things grow like crazy, huh.”
“Naofumi-san. Why are you so concerned about this?”
“Huh? Well, the kids might want a pet someday, right? Usapiru and the like are the cute type, seemed manageable, so I figured…”
“The Filolials are already around them, so surely they wouldn’t want more? And there’s Gaelion-san and the others too?”
So this was Father worrying about child-rearing, I see.
“Guess that counts as ‘already plenty’… well, I suppose the kids are so energetic the Filolials end up getting dragged around by them too.”
“Itsuki might end up with worries like this someday too,” Father murmured, I say.
“My kid seems to be leaning toward adoring Filolials, apparently… The challenge might be how to gradually wean them off that.”
“What do you mean by that?”
“The thing we need to be most careful about is the possibility of them getting a crush on Motoyasu-san, calling him a ‘handsome, rugged uncle.’”
“Ahh… Motoyasu-kun probably will turn into a handsome, rugged sort as he ages. Same goes for Ren, though.”
“No, let’s keep this one confined to just Motoyasu.”
For some reason, Ren firmly proposed narrowing it down to just me, I say.
“What about Naofumi and Itsuki, then? Try picturing your own future selves.”
“Well, when you put it that way…”
“Itsuki seems like the type whose looks won’t change much even as he ages. Still looking kind of boyish even past forty.”
“I’m a little self-conscious about that, so could you not? If we’re saying that, what about you, Naofumi-san?”
“Me? I’ll probably just turn into a pretty ordinary middle-aged guy, right? Motoyasu-kun, do you remember what our future selves look like?”
“Because of the looping, things get a bit hazy—the future appearances of you all are somewhat vague to me, I say.”
I feel like I remember at least about ten years ahead, but even then things get fuzzy in places, I say.
“Motoyasu, is anyone among us gonna go bald?”
“Ren, that’s what you’re worried about?”
“The one who seems most likely to go bald is definitely Ren-san, don’t you think? Will that guess land?”
“Quiet. Cut that kind of joke out. I’m not going bald.”
“You two, have you forgotten the getup Motoyasu-kun was wearing for a while after coming back to this loop?”
The mysterious bottle-bottom glasses and bald wig combo, I say.
“Well then, let’s settle it as: Ren-san stays non-bald, and Kurotarou-san is likely to go bald.”
“Sounds about right.”
“Why did you two settle on that!? Don’t force Itsuki’s guess to land, I say!”
That’s disrespectful to Black Thunder, I say!
“Why are we even on the topic of baldness… oh right, this was about educating our future kids.”
“On that note, Usapiru are quite hot-tempered, aren’t they? Might not be suited as a kid’s pet?”
“Depends on the breed, doesn’t it? What about the Usapiru the first-world me kept?”
“Seems it was well-trained and docile, I say. Though before becoming Raph-species, it used to fight with Filolial-sama quite often.”
“Fight? Why?”
“Probably viewed as prey, I’d guess. Pretty much survival of the fittest, wasn’t it? Imiya-san sometimes looks at Rumo-species as prey too, after all.”
Ahh… I could easily tell Father was thinking of Kou, I say.
“In the end, the safe bet’s probably the Filolials and Raph-chan and that lot—Gaelion-chan’s calmed down too, but that’s different from being a pet.”
“Even so, she does claim to be the Demon Lord of monsters.”
“She herself seems like she’d play along cutely, though. More like she’s matured, gotten better at looking after others.”
“Perhaps a Demon Lord’s duty includes looking after subordinates.”
“Demon Lord, huh… come to think of it, Gaelion-chan technically is a Demon Lord, I suppose.”
“She’s calm about it, but nothing about her usual attitude gives off that vibe at all.”
“The idea of that thing being a Demon Lord is laughable, I say.”
“Nanooon!” Gaelion protested—but as far as I’m concerned, it’s just an enemy gunning for Father, not a threat worth taking seriously, I say.
